notes.title: Chains on Sand has reached Feature Complete
notes.content: [p][i]Chains on Sand[/i] has now reached the [b]feature complete[/b] stage. All of the core systems that define the game are in place.[/p][p]Combat is at the heart of the experience: a brutal, grid-based system where every blow matters. Fighters can bleed out, be knocked to the ground, or even lose limbs in the heat of battle. Opponents don’t cheat the rules — they fight by the same mechanics the player does, each guided by distinct archetypes that shape their style and tactics.[/p][p]But survival isn’t only about the fight itself. [b]Life inside the arena[/b] means preparing carefully, managing your inventory, and choosing the right gear before stepping onto the sand. After each match, the crowd’s judgment determines whether you are celebrated, scorned, or forced to deliver a fatal blow. Over time, your victories and choices forge a reputation — merciful or ruthless, cowardly or bold.[/p][p]Not every foe is a nameless fighter. Special bosses, both hand-crafted and drawn from the legacies of past contenders, await in the dust. Defeating them is not only a test of skill, but also a step toward something greater: the chance to win your freedom.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]What’s next?[/h3][p]With all features in place, development now turns to:[/p][list][*][p]Fixing bugs and tightening the systems.[/p][/*][*][p]Polishing visuals, sound, and animations so every strike feels heavy and clear.[/p][/*][*][p]Balancing the economy, skills, and AI to keep each fight tense but fair.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]“Feature complete” means no more major systems will be added before release. From here, the focus is on sharpening what’s already built — making every duel memorable and every decision matter.[/p][p]Thank you to everyone who has followed the journey and tested the demo. Your feedback has been essential in shaping the game.[/p][p][i]Chains on Sand[/i] is getting closer to launch. The sands are thirsty. Will you rise in glory… or fall forgotten in the dust?[/p]

notes.title: Chains on Sand Demo – Combat Overhaul Update (v1.3)
notes.content:
[p]This latest update brings [b]massive improvements[/b] to the combat system, character builds, and tactical options. After weeks of iteration and community feedback, the demo now reflects what is likely to be the [b]final version of the combat rules[/b] for Chains on Sand.[/p][hr][/hr][h3] Core Combat Changes[/h3][list][*][p][b] New Stun Mechanic[/b]
A successful blow can now [b]stagger your opponent[/b], denying them actions. Use it to break momentum — or suffer it when you drop your guard.[/p][/*][*][p][b] Offhand Attacks Introduced[/b]
Fighters with the right training can now perform [b]offhand attacks[/b], allowing true dual wielding or shield bashes.[/p][/*][*][p][b] New Maneuvers[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Riposte[/b] – A defensive stance that counters incoming attacks.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Illusive Attack[/b] – A feint that lowers defenses.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Defensive Attack[/b] – Attack while staying safe and focused.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3] Character Building Overhaul[/h3][list][*][p][b]Universal Skill Costs[/b]
All skills now cost a [b]flat 5 XP per level[/b] — simplifying planning and balancing character builds.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Consumables Introduced[/b]
Healing salves, thrown flasks, and other limited-use items are now in the loot pool. (They may appear more frequently in later fights.)[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3] Bug Fixes & Stability[/h3][list][*][p]Many long-standing bugs were squashed.[/p][/*][*][p]AI behavior is now more responsive and fair.[/p][/*][*][p]Loot transfer and display are now reliable.[/p][/*][*][p]Major systems were refactored to prepare for polish phase.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3] Leaderboard Reset[/h3][p]Due to the [b]new combat rules and balance changes[/b], the leaderboard has been [b]reset[/b]. All contenders must now prove themselves under the new rules. Here is the last one for the records - congratulations to the champions![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45620697/453e6050ca98e444cac4356c8c71102360f9ecb7.png"][/img][/p][hr][/hr][h3] Legacy Bosses[/h3][p]Some legacy bosses may now appear again in the arena. Enemies that kill your characters may be upgraded to legacy bosses and appear on future runs.[/p][p][/p][h3] Demo Roadmap[/h3][p]This version likely reflects the [b]finalized combat rules[/b] for Chains on Sand. However:[/p][list][*][p]A [b]final demo version[/b] will follow later, focused on [b]visual polish[/b], better animations, and presentation improvements.[/p][/*][*][p]Minor bugfixing updates may still appear before that final demo.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3] We Want Your Feedback[/h3][p]Your victories, deaths, and feedback are what shape this game. If you played an earlier version, now is the time to return — the arena is more brutal and rewarding than ever.[/p]

notes.title: Demo Release Imminent!
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

I’m excited to announce that the first playable demo of Chains on Sand is almost here! After months of development and feedback from testers, I’m preparing to open the doors for you to experience the gritty tactical combat at the heart of the game.

[h3]What Can You Expect?[/h3]
15 rounds of brutal, turn-based arena battles—build your contender, fight for survival, and earn your freedom (or fall to the sands).

[b]Deep tactical combat[/b] with stamina, crippling injuries, weapon reach, armor, magic, and meaningful crowd decisions.

[b]Procedural opponents[/b]: Every enemy is unique, with different archetypes, weapons, and strategies.

[b]Paperdoll equipment system[/b]: Swap weapons, shields, armor, and see them on your character.

[b]Item looting[/b] and durability: Take gear from fallen foes (and watch it break!).

[b]Character progression[/b]: Level up between fights, spend XP, unlock skills and traits.

[b]Reputation and crowd judgment[/b]: The crowd will remember your mercy (or cruelty).

[h3]Please Note:[/h3]
Most of the art is placeholder and many UI elements are still work-in-progress.

Some features, such as the town/rest phase and legendary challenges, are not in the demo yet.

Sound, music, and certain visual effects are being refined—expect rough edges!

But the core combat system is already deep and rewarding. You’ll get a real taste of the tense decision-making and consequences that define Chains on Sand.

[h3]Estimated Playtime[/h3]
The demo offers about 15 arena rounds, enough for several runs and plenty of emergent moments.

I can’t wait to see your feedback and stories from the arena. Thank you for checking out the game—your input will help shape the final release!

[i]Add Chains on Sand to your wishlist to support the project, and let me know what you think after you try the demo![/i]

notes.title: Devlog: Meet the Smarter Arena AI!
notes.content:
Hello!

I’m excited to share one of the biggest updates yet: a complete overhaul of the enemy AI system. Every enemy you fight now thinks—and fights—differently, using unique tactics and personalities based on their archetype. Here’s a peek under the hood at how it works, and what you can expect in your next arena brawl:

[h1][b]How the New AI Works[/b][/h1]
Each enemy now belongs to an archetype—think of it as a combat “personality.” Instead of every enemy acting the same, their decisions are driven by a set of priorities, preferred maneuvers, and even quirks. This makes each match more unpredictable and challenging.

[b][h3]Archetype Highlights[/h3][/b]
[b]Brute[/b]
The Brute charges in with no fear, using all their strength to overwhelm you. Expect relentless Total Attacks and double strikes, with little care for defense or cleverness. If you can’t outlast them, you’ll be trampled.

[b]Rogue[/b]
Rogues are fast, tricky, and hate being pinned down. They prefer hit-and-run tactics, flanking, and escaping if things get too hot. If you’re not careful, they’ll bleed you dry before you can even get a solid hit in.

[b]Guardian[/b]
The Guardian is the fortress. Heavy armor, a big shield, and patience—they wait for you to make a mistake, defending constantly and striking only to cripple or punish aggression.

[b]Knight[/b]
Knights are a balanced mix of power and discipline. They press their advantage aggressively but will switch to defense if the tides turn. Don’t expect them to back down just because you’re ready for an attack.

[b]Hunter[/b]
The master of distance, the Hunter kites you around the arena, firing from afar and only panicking if you close in. They’ll try to keep you at arm’s length as long as their arrows last.

[b]Sentinel[/b]
Sentinels specialize in polearms and keeping you away. They maintain their reach, use the Ready action for opportunity attacks, and fall back on backup weapons or defense if you get too close.

[b]Duelist[/b]
Duelists are all about rhythm and precision—mixing feints, aggressive combos, and careful retreats. If they have the upper hand, expect a flurry of blows. If not, they’ll play defensively and look for their moment.

[b]Monk[/b]
Monks are relentless. They’ll try to disarm you, cripple your limbs, grapple to keep you from escaping, and alternate between punches and kicks. Don’t let them get in close!

[b]Healer[/b]: Focuses on self-buffing and healing, playing defensively, and only attacking when fully prepared.

[b]Elementalist[/b]: Uses long-range spells, tries to control the battlefield with area effects and status, and keeps their distance at all costs.

[b]Controller: [/b]Specializes in debuffs and area denial—weakening you before going for the kill.

[b]Battle Mage:[/b] Starts by stacking buffs, then charges into melee like an armored brute, using magic to boost strength and resilience.

[h3][b]What This Means for You[/b][/h3]
Every enemy is now more than just a stat block—they have a strategy.
Some will test your defenses. Some will try to wear you down or outmaneuver you. And some will punish you for every mistake.

This update makes every fight feel unique, and I’m eager to hear which archetype gives you the most trouble—or which one is your favorite to beat!

As always, your feedback is super valuable—if you see enemies doing something weird or have ideas for even cooler AI tactics, let me know in the comments or the community page.

Back to the arena,
ChainsOnSand Dev

notes.title: What to Expect for Chains on Sand
notes.content:
Hi contenders,

I wanted to share some quick news and set your expectations for the road ahead!

[b]Release Window:[/b]
I’m aiming for an August release for Chains on Sand. I haven’t decided yet whether it will be a full launch or an Early Access release—but if it starts in Early Access, it won’t stay there for long. The main goal is to polish the experience, squash bugs, and make sure the core gameplay feels as satisfying (and brutal) as it should.

[b]Demo Before Launch:[/b]
Before release, there will be a public demo so everyone can get a taste of the arena—test the combat, character creation, and some of the early progression. Your feedback will help shape the final experience and make the game better.

[b]What’s Next:[/b]
I’ll be posting regular updates as we get closer to release—showing new features, behind-the-scenes development, and hopefully getting your input on balance and ideas.

Thank you so much to everyone who’s wishlisted and followed the project so far! If you know anyone who loves tactical roguelikes or gladiator games, please share the page—it really helps!

Let me know what you want to see or test in the demo.
See you in the sand!
